"""Regression tests for ``boltons.strutils.ordinalize``.

A regression made the function select the ordinal suffix based on the
*tens* digit being 2 instead of 1. That gave teens (11-19, which always
take ``th``) the ``st``/``nd``/``rd`` suffix of their final digit, and
stripped ``st``/``nd``/``rd`` from numbers ending in the twenties
(21, 22, 23). These tests pin the standard English rules:

* the last two digits in 11-19 take ``th``;
* otherwise the suffix follows the final digit (1 -> st, 2 -> nd,
  3 -> rd, anything else -> th);
* a trailing non-digit leaves the value unchanged (and yields an empty
  suffix when ``ext_only=True``).
"""

import pytest

from boltons.strutils import ordinalize


LAST_DIGIT_CASES = [
    (0, '0th'),
    (1, '1st'),
    (2, '2nd'),
    (3, '3rd'),
    (4, '4th'),
    (5, '5th'),
    (6, '6th'),
    (7, '7th'),
    (8, '8th'),
    (9, '9th'),
]

TEEN_CASES = [(n, f'{n}th') for n in range(10, 20)]

TWENTIES_CASES = [
    (20, '20th'),
    (21, '21st'),
    (22, '22nd'),
    (23, '23rd'),
    (24, '24th'),
    (25, '25th'),
    (26, '26th'),
    (27, '27th'),
    (28, '28th'),
    (29, '29th'),
]

OTHER_TENS_CASES = [
    (30, '30th'),
    (31, '31st'),
    (32, '32nd'),
    (33, '33rd'),
    (34, '34th'),
    (40, '40th'),
    (51, '51st'),
    (62, '62nd'),
    (73, '73rd'),
    (84, '84th'),
    (95, '95th'),
    (100, '100th'),
    (101, '101st'),
    (102, '102nd'),
    (103, '103rd'),
    (104, '104th'),
]

LARGER_NUMBER_CASES = [
    # the teen rule keys off the last two digits at any magnitude
    (111, '111th'),
    (112, '112th'),
    (113, '113th'),
    (114, '114th'),
    (211, '211th'),
    (1011, '1011th'),
    (2013, '2013th'),
    (3694839230, '3694839230th'),
    # ...and the twenties rule must not swallow numbers ending in 21-23
    (121, '121st'),
    (122, '122nd'),
    (123, '123rd'),
    (124, '124th'),
    (221, '221st'),
    (222, '222nd'),
    (223, '223rd'),
    (1001, '1001st'),
    (1002, '1002nd'),
    (1003, '1003rd'),
]

NON_DIGIT_CASES = ['hi', '', '123abc', 'no. 1!', ' 4 ']


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', LAST_DIGIT_CASES)
def test_single_digits(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', TEEN_CASES)
def test_teens_take_th(number, expected):
    # Regression: 11, 12, 13 used to come out as 11st, 12nd, 13rd.
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', TWENTIES_CASES)
def test_twenties_follow_final_digit(number, expected):
    # Regression: 21, 22, 23 used to come out as 21th, 22th, 23th.
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', OTHER_TENS_CASES)
def test_other_numbers(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', LARGER_NUMBER_CASES)
def test_teen_and_twenties_rules_apply_to_last_two_digits(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', TEEN_CASES + TWENTIES_CASES)
def test_ext_only_returns_suffix_for_digit_endings(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number, ext_only=True) == expected[-2:]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number', TEEN_CASES + TWENTIES_CASES)
def test_ext_only_suffix_equals_full_result_minus_number(number):
    assert ordinalize(number, ext_only=True) == ordinalize(number)[len(str(number)):]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('text', NON_DIGIT_CASES)
def test_non_digit_endings_are_unchanged(text):
    # Regression guard for the documented fallback: no digit at the end
    # means the input is passed through as-is.
    assert ordinalize(text) == text
    assert ordinalize(text, ext_only=True) == ''


def test_string_digit_input_is_supported():
    assert ordinalize('11') == '11th'
    assert ordinalize('22') == '22nd'
    assert ordinalize('22', ext_only=True) == 'nd'


def test_negative_numbers_follow_last_two_digits():
    assert ordinalize(-1) == '-1st'
    assert ordinalize(-2) == '-2nd'
    assert ordinalize(-3) == '-3rd'
    assert ordinalize(-4) == '-4th'
    assert ordinalize(-11) == '-11th'
    assert ordinalize(-12) == '-12th'
    assert ordinalize(-13) == '-13th'
    assert ordinalize(-21) == '-21st'
    assert ordinalize(-22) == '-22nd'
    assert ordinalize(-23) == '-23rd'
